# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old during Volume 2  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Welby  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mother Rosalind  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a tiny woman with thick, lovely, wavy snow-white hair styled in flattering puffs and coils. Beneath her hair, she has a youthful face with rosy cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and large, gentle, wood-brown eyes filled with tiny flecks of gold. She favors delicate dresses, such as cream muslin with roses or forget-me-not organdy, adorned with frills and laces.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022), [v2 c28 P57](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0057)_

## Personality

Rosalind is romantic, imaginative, and youthful in spirit, frequently engaging in lighthearted play and pretending. Despite her whimsical nature and love of solitude, she is deeply practical, hospitable, and warm-hearted. She despises the thought of advancing in age and resists social expectations of conventional old maidenhood. She possesses a voice that evokes satin, splashing water, and fairy bells.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and fond of pretending  <sub>[v2 c21 P55](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0055), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- Resentful of growing old  <sub>[v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>
- Hospitable  <sub>[v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058), [v2 c21 P64](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0064), [v2 c27 P27](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0027)</sub>
- Dislikes social obligations and formal visiting  <sub>[v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c27 P48](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0048)</sub>
- Dislikes dahlias

## Abilities

- Baking and cooking lavish spreads  <sub>[v2 c21 P64](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0064), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c27 P27](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0027)</sub>
- Entertaining with woodland echoes  <sub>[v2 c21 P71](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0071), [v2 c21 P74](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0074)</sub>

## Goals

- To retain her youthful spirit and live on her own terms  <sub>[v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose lived a secluded, quiet life at Echo Cottage, a small stone house in Welby built by her grandfather eight decades earlier. One autumn day, Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon Echo Cottage and struck up a delightful acquaintance with her and her handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth. Nell quickly became a close friend and kindred spirit, visiting frequently to share in imaginative games, tea parties, and talks. Through Nell, Rosalind met Cedric Stanhope, the son of her former fiancé Stephen Stanhope, and formed a warm maternal bond with the young boy. After Stephen Stanhope returned to the area and sent word through Nell that he wished to see her, he visited Echo Cottage, leading to their reconciliation. They were married in late August beneath the garden's honeysuckle trellis—the exact spot where Stephen had proposed twenty-five years earlier—and departed for Boston and a trip to the Pacific coast. They continue to return to Echo Cottage each summer with Cedric and Belinda the Fourth to enjoy the season.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c28 P35](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0035), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c29 P10](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0010), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c23 P2](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0002), [v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Named Rosalind by her father because he loved the fragrance of lavender, which had kept him awake thinking of her mother when they first met  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Lost her mother a decade prior to Volume 2, after which she took in young local girls named Bowman as handmaidens in exchange for room, board, and garments  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Was betrothed in her youth to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years before Volume 2, but parted from him following a disagreement  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>

## Quotes

> Belinda the Fourth mentioned that you wanted to speak with me  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046)</sub>

> Is it all right if I act as though our acquaintance goes back a century and address you as Nell and Isolde from this moment on?  <sub>[v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062)</sub>

> I always prefer to execute things as thoroughly as I can, and because it was my fate to become an old maid, I resolved that I would be an exceptionally pleasant one.  <sub>[v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015)</sub>

> Thus this is the son of Stephen  <sub>[v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027)</sub>
